verdict.rationale: Microsoft documents a public Teams API through Microsoft Graph. External services can call it to automate Teams: creating teams, adding members, configuring channels, tabs and apps, posting channel messages, and exporting chat content. One community report notes that integration needs the full Azure/Graph stack, which is a complexity caveat rather than a contradiction. missing for 10: a discoverable machine-readable OpenAPI spec (probes returned 404), independent hands-on corroboration of agent-driven API use, and documented auth and rate-limit details in the pack.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: You can create websites, services, and native platform applications that run outside the Microsoft Teams user experience, and call the Teams API to automate Teams scenarios.
Send a new [chatMessage](resources/chatmessage?view=graph-rest-1.0) in the specified [channel](resources/channel?view=graph-rest-1.0).
Use Microsoft Graph to create a new virtual team when a new business issue arises, add the right people to the team, and configure the team with channels, tabs, and apps.
Teams Export APIs allow you to export 1:1, group chat, meeting chats, and channel messages from Microsoft Teams.
